description: Table 5 is a single image panel: a five-column, five-row data table titled "The equilibrium distribution coefficient and diffusion coefficient". The column headers, exactly as printed, are Element, k(δ), D^δ/[cm² s⁻¹], k(γ) and D^γ/[cm² s⁻¹]; the row labels are the elements Al, N, Mn, S and Ti. The k columns are printed as bare dimensionless numbers, given for the δ and γ phases respectively: Al 0.6/0.6, N 0.25/0.48, Mn 0.77/0.785, S 0.05/0.035 and Ti 0.38/0.33. Every D entry is an Arrhenius expression of the form A·exp(−Q/RT) with units cm² s⁻¹: Al 5.9exp(−241417/RT) in both phases; N 0.008exp(−79078/RT) in δ versus 0.91exp(−168490/RT) in γ; Mn 0.76exp(−224430/RT) versus 0.055exp(−249366/RT); S 4.56exp(−214639/RT) versus 2.4exp(−223426/RT); Ti 3.15exp(−247693/RT) versus 0.15exp(−250956/RT). There are no plotted curves, micrographs or scale bars. The table supplies the thermodynamic input parameters (equilibrium partition coefficients and diffusion coefficients in δ-ferrite and γ-austenite) needed to model microsegregation and inclusion precipitation during solidification; Al is the only element whose k and D are identical in the two phases.

observations.observation: The table image has five columns headed Element, k(δ), D^δ/[cm² s⁻¹], k(γ) and D^γ/[cm² s⁻¹], indicating partition coefficients and diffusion coefficients for the δ and γ phases separately.
The five data rows are the elements Al, N, Mn, S and Ti.
Al is the only element with identical values in both phases: k(δ) = 0.6 and k(γ) = 0.6, and the same diffusion expression 5.9exp(−241417/RT) in δ and γ.
Nitrogen has k(δ) = 0.25 versus k(γ) = 0.48, and D^δ = 0.008exp(−79078/RT) versus D^γ = 0.91exp(−168490/RT).
Mn has k(δ) = 0.77 versus k(γ) = 0.785, and D^δ = 0.76exp(−224430/RT) versus D^γ = 0.055exp(−249366/RT).
S has k(δ) = 0.05 versus k(γ) = 0.035, and D^δ = 4.56exp(−214639/RT) versus D^γ = 2.4exp(−223426/RT).
Ti has k(δ) = 0.38 versus k(γ) = 0.33, and D^δ = 3.15exp(−247693/RT) versus D^γ = 0.15exp(−250956/RT).

Every diffusion coefficient is printed as an Arrhenius form A·exp(−Q/RT) with A quoted to 1-3 significant figures and Q as a bare number; the unit of Q and the gas-constant convention are not printed in the table.
The caption states the table gives the equilibrium distribution coefficient and diffusion coefficient and cites references [42-44].
The citing text states that the k and D values of Table 5 are used together with the solidification time t_f and the secondary dendrite arm spacing λ in a microsegregation expression.
The table contains no values or rows for the alloy's C or Fe, so the tabulated elements are the ones treated as solutes in the solidification model.
